items.cite: John Cage, *Silence: Lectures and Writings*, 50th anniversary edition (Wesleyan University Press, 2013).
items.note: Cage’s own lectures and essays, and the starting point for his treatment of silence, composition and the performance of a text. The date is that of the anniversary paperback linked here.

items.cite: James Pritchett, *The Music of John Cage* (Cambridge University Press, 1993).
items.note: Explains the compositional work behind the ideas, especially the difference between using chance to make a score and leaving decisions to performers.

items.cite: John Cage, *The Selected Letters of John Cage*, edited by Laura Kuhn (Wesleyan University Press, 2016).
items.note: Correspondence. Useful for tracing the people, practical requests and artistic exchanges behind Cage’s works, and as a check on the familiar anecdotes.

items.cite: Kenneth Silverman, *Begin Again: A Biography of John Cage* (Northwestern University Press, 2012).
items.note: A substantial account of Cage’s life among musicians, dancers, artists and friends. This citation identifies the checked Northwestern paperback edition.
